title: List colouring
description: List assignments from which a graph cannot be properly coloured: they refute choosability, which is Pi-2-complete once lists of size 3 occur (Erdos, Rubin and Taylor; Gutner and Tarsi). The abstraction guesses the lists, the check finds a colouring from them, and the refinement says that one node loses the colour it was given. The default is K(3,3) with lists of size 2, an easy case; try a = 2, b = 4, p = 4 (144 solutions).

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The graph, the palette and the list sizes. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.
% The palette, and size(V,K): the list of node V has K colours.
% (Mix sizes 2 and 3 for the hard case, for example: size(1,3). size(V,2) :- node(V), V > 1.)
colour(1..p).
size(V,2) :- node(V).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): a list of colours for every node.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a list of the required size for every node.
K { list(V,C) : colour(C) } K :- size(V,K).
#show list/2.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a proper colouring from the lists (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: a proper colouring that gives every node a colour from its list.
1 { col(V,C) : list(V,C) } 1 :- node(V).
:- edge(U,V), col(U,C), col(V,C).
#show col/2.

% The colouring works for all lists that still contain the colours it uses.
relevant(list(V,C)) :- col(V,C).

fragments.name: view
fragments.text:
% One row per node, one column per colour: the lists of the candidate; a colouring ringed.
#program scene.
draw(layout(grid)).
draw(cell(V,C)) :- node(V), colour(C).

#program frame.
draw(attr(cell(V,C), fill, list)) :- cand(list(V,C)).
draw(attr(cell(V,C), label, "x")) :- cex(col(V,C)).
draw(emph(cell(V,C))) :- lit(list(V,C), _).
draw(note("A proper colouring from the lists (x): one of its ringed colours must leave a list.")) :- kind(reject).
#show draw/1.
fragments.description: A domain view (Observatory tab): the scene part draws what stays, the frame part one step, as draw/1 marks.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts:
% The complete bipartite graph with a nodes on the left and b nodes on the right.
left(1..a).
right(a+1..a+b).
node(V) :- left(V).
node(V) :- right(V).
edge(U,V) :- left(U), right(V).

% K(2,4) with lists of 2 out of 4 colours.
left(1..a).
right(a+1..a+b).
node(V) :- left(V).
node(V) :- right(V).
edge(U,V) :- left(U), right(V).

% The 5-cycle, lists of 2 out of 3 colours: an odd cycle is not 2-choosable.
node(1..5).
edge(I,I+1) :- I = 1..4.  edge(1,5).

% The 6-cycle, lists of 2 out of 3 colours: every even cycle is 2-choosable, so there is no solution.
node(1..6).
edge(I,I+1) :- I = 1..5.  edge(1,6).

% The theta graph with paths of lengths 2, 2 and 4 between nodes 1 and 2, lists of 2 out of 3 colours:
% 2-choosable (Erdos, Rubin and Taylor), so there is no solution.
node(1..7).
edge(1,3). edge(3,2). edge(1,4). edge(4,2).
edge(1,5). edge(5,6). edge(6,7). edge(7,2).

generators.name: gnp
generators.description: A connected random graph G(n,p): each edge with probability p/1000; a disconnected draw is redrawn.
generators.text:
% gnp: a connected random graph with n nodes; each edge is present with probability p/1000
node(1..n).
edge(X,Y) :- node(X), node(Y), X < Y, @flip(p, X, Y) = 1.

reach(1).
reach(Y) :- reach(X), edge(X,Y).
reach(X) :- reach(Y), edge(X,Y).
:- node(X), not reach(X).            % a disconnected draw is rejected and redrawn

#show node/1.  #show edge/2.

generators.name: gnm
generators.description: A random graph G(n,m): exactly m of the n(n-1)/2 possible edges, chosen uniformly.
generators.text:
% gnm: m edges chosen uniformly among the pairs of n nodes (pair I is the I-th pair X < Y)
node(1..n).
pair(X,Y,(X-1)*n - (X-1)*X/2 + Y - X) :- node(X), node(Y), X < Y.
edge(X,Y) :- pair(X,Y,I), @subset(m, n*(n-1)/2, I, edges) = 1.

#show node/1.  #show edge/2.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 5):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + abstraction   options "--enum-mode=record"
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

spaces.name: graphs
spaces.description: Every graph on size nodes, lists of 2 out of p colours.
spaces.text:
% every graph on the nodes 1..size (edges listed in both directions)
node(1..size).
{ edge(U,V) : node(U), node(V), U < V }.
edge(V,U) :- edge(U,V), U < V.
